Life expectancy from rates or forecast draws

Source: R/derive-lifetable.R
life_expectancy.Rd

Life expectancy of the period life table of life_table() (Preston, Heuveline and Guillot 2001), for draws path by path.

Usage

life_expectancy(
  x,
  age = NULL,
  at = NULL,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.975),
  paths = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A matrix or array of rates with age in the first dimension, an mt_draws object, or an mt_data object (observed rates with Poisson intervals, see mt_observed()).

age

An mt_axis (taken from x for draws).

at

Age at which life expectancy is computed (start of an interval; default the first age).

probs

Quantiles reported for draws.

paths

For draws, return the values of every path, an array [period, stratum, draw].

...

Passed to the life-table calculation (ax, open, k, omega). A rate of 0 in the open interval is replaced as in life_table().

Value

For arrays, an array without the age dimension. For draws, a data.table with the mean and quantiles per stratum and period, computed path by path.

References

Preston SH, Heuveline P, Guillot M (2001). Demography: Measuring and Modeling Population Processes. Blackwell.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
m <- mt_array(x, "deaths") / mt_array(x, "exposure")
life_expectancy(m, mt_grid(x)$age, at = 65)[1:3, ]
#>       stratum
#> period   female     male
#>   1990 21.17552 16.96333
#>   1991 21.28877 16.89039
#>   1992 21.36637 16.94218
